limitations: Counts concern source fidelity, not clinical truth, diagnostic accuracy, safety or guideline concordance.
Negative lexical candidates were reviewed semantically; lexical counts must not be treated as a clinical fidelity rate.
Qualified epistemic claims remain ambiguous where the source does not resolve their scope.
Numeric novelty screening alone cannot establish narrative fidelity.
Positive narrative assertions and doctor reasoning were not exhaustively clinically adjudicated.
Tool-output checks cover logged distinct excerpts and recorded prerequisite chronology; they are not independent medical review.
No finding was used for retuning or outcome reclassification.
